questions.question:

options.text: Someone who makes the right decision

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Someone who resembles their parent.

• The most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'Chip off the old block' is 'Someone who resembles their parent.'
 
• Chip off the old block: someone who is very similar in character to their father or mother.

Correct meaning:__ *Someone who resembles their parent*.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He ran __most happily__ to receive his father.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is-'happily'.

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• Use of adverb: It is a word that modifies (describes) a verb, an adjective, another adverb, or even a whole sentence.
 
• **happily: ***It is the adverb form of '**happy**'.
 
• We **do not use** most, more before an adverb.
 
• Hence, the most appropriate option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words 'most happily' is 'happily'.
 
• Thus, *option 1) *is the correct answer.

 

Correct Sentence: *He ran **happily__** to receive his father.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's see other option:
 
 
• **happier**: it is comparative degree of '**happy**'
 
• **happy**: feeling or showing pleasure; pleased
 
• **more happily**: we **do not** use '**more**' before an adverb

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Intelligent and strikingly attractive, Tess is indisputably the central character of the novel that bears her name.

B. But she is also more than a distinctive individual: Hardy makes her into somewhat of a mythic heroine.

C. Her name, formally Theresa, recalls St. Teresa of Avila, another martyr whose vision of a higher reality cost her, her life.

D. Tess’s story, thus, is a story representing a deeper and larger experience than that of a single individual.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**ABCD'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Sentence A** introduced the noun, **Tess**. So it is the **first** sentence.
 
• **Sentence B** tell **about a trait of his character**. So it is the **second** sentence.
 
• **Sentence C** twists the sentence **towards another martyr, ****St. Teresa of Avila**. It is **third** sentence.
 
• **Sentence D concludes the whole story**. So, it is the **fourth** sentence. 

Hence, '**option 4**' is the correct answer.

questions.question:

__
 
• The most appropriate synonym of the given word 'robbed' is 'plundered'.
 
• robbed: to take money, property, etc. from a person or place illegally.
 
• Meaning of the given options:
 
 
• conquered: to take **control of a country or city and its people by force**, especially in a war
 
• *plundered: **to take the goods of by force** (as in war)*
 
• annexed: to take **control of another country** or region by force
 
• attacked*: *to try to **hurt or defeat somebody**/something by using force*.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 2.​

questions.question:

The mob / is believing / every word / the leader says.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The error lies in 'is believing' part of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence should be written in Simple present tense and in Active Voice.
 
• We use the simple present tense when an action** happens regularly.**
 
• Structure: Subject + V1 + s/es(if singular subject) + object (Active Voice)__
 __
 
• *​Example: He plays football. (Active Voice)*
 
 
 
• V1 form of 'believing' is 'believe'.
 
• Subject of the sentence (The mob) is singular, hence we will use 's/es' with V1.
 
• Therefore, the use of 'is believing' should be replaced with 'believes' to make it grammatically correct.

 

Correct sentence__: *The mob __**believes**__ every word the leader says.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Parker has been bitten by a rare species of spiders.

options.text: A rare species of spiders had bitten Parker.
A rare species of spiders is biting Parker.
A rare species of spiders has bitten Parker.
A rare species of spiders bit Parker.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'A rare species of spiders has bitten Parker.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Present perfect Tense and in Passive Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a sentence in present perfect Tense from Passive voice to Active voice:
 
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e., the object of the passive sentence becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• The active voice starts with the object of the passive voice.
 
• Structure: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject (____Passive____ Voice)__
 
 

 Subject + has/have + V3 + Object __(Active Voice)__ 

__
 
• Solution: *Parker has been bitten by a rare species of spiders. *(Passive Voice)

 * A rare species of spiders has bitten Parker. *(Active Voice)

 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'A rare species of spiders has bitten Parker.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, the sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: *He reads a novel. *(Active Voice)

 *A novel is read by him. *(Passive Voice)

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error

Investing on real estate / can earn you quick profit / but it comes with / a certain amount of risk attached to it.

options.text: a certain amount of risk attached to it

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Investing on real estate.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in 'Investing on real estate' part of the sentence.
 
• Use of On: To indicate touching and being supported by the top surface of (something), or moving to a position that is supported by something.
 
 
• *Example: The book is lying on the table.*
 
 
 
• *​*Use of In: That someone or something belongs to or is included as part of something.
 
 
• *Example: She used to play in a band. *
 
 
 
• Therefore, the use of 'Investing on real estate' should be replaced with 'Investing in real estate' to make it grammatically correct.

 

Correct sentence__: ***__Investing in real estate__** can earn you quick profit but it comes with a certain amount of risk attached to it.*

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• "**Around**" means "**to various places**".

• **Example**: *The Evans are **moving around** India for Summer vacation. *
 
 
 
• "**Moving into**" means "**entering into**".
 
 
• **Example: ***We will be **moving into** our new flat within a month. *
 
 
 
• Therefore, the appropriate option is "is now moving into".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's see some phrasal verbs beginning with "**move**". 
 
• **Moving along** - progressing or developing.
 
 
• **Example:** *I am **moving along** the story.*
 
 
 
• **Moving at** - set into motion.
 
 
• **Example:** *The train is **moving at** a speed of 100kmph. *
 
 
 
• **Moving on **- going forward
 
 
• **Example:** *Rin needs to **move on** from his current job. *
 
 
 
• **move over** - go aside.
 
 
• **Example**:* I want to sit here. Please **move over. ***
